text:
leo: Heads up, publishing stuck because SDK regen flipped a typehash in the go sampleapp. Auth/retry parity tests failing in CI.
ci-bot: build #842 failed · regendiff summary: example ordering changed in `CreateUser` -> typehash mismatch. See: https://ci.internal/842/regendiff 
ana: That openapi tweak that reordered `examples` was a tiny cleanup, didn't expect it to ripple.
devon: FYI typegen uses the YAML/JSON canonical representation for hashing. Small ordering/whitespace diffs should not change the hash, but looks like a regression in the canonicalizer.
leo: Can we gate the release so we don't force a semver-major suggestion from the changelog bot? It bumped to major because it detected "API surface change".
ops-bot: release-bot: semver-suggest => MAJOR (changed: examples.CreateUser order).
riley: short-term: we can revert the examples reorder in the sampleapp repo to unblock publish. Long-term: fix canonicalization and add a regen CI test to detect order-only diffs.
devon: I'll open a patch to the canonicalizer: sort example keys deterministically and normalize description whitespace before computing the typehash. Adds < 30 LOC.
nana: also add a unit test that runs regen on the sampleapp with only example ordering changed and asserts typehash unchanged.
leo: will do the temporary revert + escalate to the release team to skip the suggested semver bump for this run.
ci-bot: note: restarting blocked builds after revert recommended.
leo: thanks all, let's track the follow-ups in the repo issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/issues/204
devon: assigning to self for canonicalizer patch, will PR today.
riley: I'll update release-bot to ignore example-only diffs for semver hints and add a note in the release playbook.
nana: great. small paper cuts like this keep tripping publishing flow. :facepalm:
